clauses.claim: The target is the unrestricted finite-rank minimal regular-cover question.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Read the exact formulations. Neither imposes finiteness on the regular covers. Finite minimal-cover multiplicity remains a separate question.

clauses.claim: Unbased regular covers correspond exactly to admissible normal subgroups N contained in the monodromy kernel K.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Normality makes N independent of the chosen flag and turns containment in any conjugate flag stabilizer into containment in its core. Rank-preserving isomorphisms commute with every coloured adjacency and cannot identify distinct N.

clauses.claim: Maximal admissible normal subgroups exist above each admissible subgroup.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: The set of subgroups of fixed W is a set. Each finite intersection witness modulo a chain union already occurs in a chain member.

clauses.claim: A relation of actual flag actions supported on disjoint rank sets splits into trivial actions.
retained_inputs: Flags are determined by their faces; each distinguished adjacency changes only its own rank
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Use the inverse action outside the other support to fix each coordinate. An arbitrary involution-generated string group is not substituted for an actual flag action.

clauses.claim: Cyclically reduced interval-supported relations of length at least two normally generate K.
retained_inputs: CH: Lemmas3.1–3.3, Definition3.5, equation3.1, PDF pp12–13
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Apply C04 to disjoint pure factors. Connected components of support in the noncommutation path are intervals. Singleton factors cannot lie in K. Conjugate back after cyclic reduction.

clauses.claim: The free extension at either end of a string C-group is a string C-group.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Identify H*_A(A×C2), its other maximal parabolic B*_C(C×C2), and their intersection B by reduced normal forms. Induct and reverse the indexing for the other end.

clauses.claim: All nonempty-generator standard parabolic cosets form a factor system with threshold one.
retained_inputs: BHS: Lemmas2.4/2.6, Definition8.1, PDF pp14–15 and26
Standard Davis cubical realization and graph-product convexity
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Exclude vertices. Closest-pair product bridges give the exact gate parabolic with label set I intersect J intersect common-link(T); empty label set gives the allowed zero-diameter gate. Prove the required hyperplane-parallel copies and uniform local multiplicity.

clauses.claim: The union of a parallel class is the coset of V_(I union link(I)), hence is proper for nonempty proper I.
retained_inputs: BHS: convex bridge and parallelism definitions
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: A shortest separating path has common-link labels when the whole parabolic is its gate image; conversely commuting strips yield every copy. Connected noncommutation makes I union link(I) proper.

clauses.claim: The factored contact graph is equivariantly quasi-isometric to the Cayley graph generated by all proper parabolics.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Give g↦gH_s with upper constant four. Associate carriers to ordinary vertices and full parallel-class unions to cone vertices; each associated set has Cayley diameter one and consecutive sets intersect. This supplies the reverse inequality and coarse surjectivity.

clauses.claim: That Cayley graph is hyperbolic and its action acylindrical.
retained_inputs: BHS: Proposition8.25 PDF p36; Corollary14.5 PDF pp66–67
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Check proper cocompact invariant cubical action, the factor system, and transfer acylindricity via the explicit equivariant metric inequalities. No arbitrary quasi-isometry invariance of an action is asserted.

clauses.claim: Every nonzero power of a full-support cyclically reduced word has the same primitive infinite cyclic centralizer.
retained_inputs: CH: Theorem3.7 PDF pp13–15; pure-factor normal forms
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Connected noncommutation gives one infinite pure factor, and full support leaves no commuting-link subgroup.

clauses.claim: Such a word has a contracting periodic Davis axis.
retained_inputs: CF: Corollary4.6(ii), PDF p11; Davis setup p9
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: C11 gives the virtually cyclic centralizer criterion for rank one. Apply contraction to the proper CAT(0) periodic axis in the cubical Davis metric.

clauses.claim: The axis has uniformly bounded coarse intersections with every proper parabolic coset.
retained_inputs: Graph-product hyperplane labels and the cubical d1/d2 comparison
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Each coset misses a generator label. A periodic reduced segment crosses at least one distinct missing-label wall per period. None crosses the coset, so endpoint-to-coset distances bound the number of periods uniformly.

clauses.claim: The projections of all proper cosets to the axis have uniformly bounded diameter.
retained_inputs: BF: Lemma3.2 PDF pp6–7; Corollary3.4 PDF p8
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Apply the close-pair estimate to two separated end subintervals, not to the whole joining segment. C13 bounds the separation of the resulting two axis points. This proves loxodromicity in the coned Cayley graph.

clauses.claim: The elementary subgroup is hyperbolically embedded relative to this same infinite generating set.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: C10 and C14 provide hyperbolicity and loxodromic WPD for the precise Cayley action used by the theorem. The retained conclusion preserves that generating set.

clauses.claim: Every cyclic power subgroup is normal in the elementary subgroup; all sufficiently large integer powers meet the filling depth condition.
retained_inputs: DGO: Lemma6.5 and Corollary6.6(b), PDF pp86–89; proper relative metric and depth definition p126
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Conjugation of some power to itself or its inverse normalizes its common primitive cyclic centralizer, acting by sign. Every power subgroup is therefore normal. Finite relative balls meet only finitely many powers, so the condition holds for all sufficiently large exponents, not merely a progression.

clauses.claim: The high-power quotient preserves the entire union of proper parabolics and hence all intersection identities.
retained_inputs: DGO: Theorem7.15(c), PDF p127; injection proof p131; Corollary4.27 PDF p48
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: The injection conclusion applies to the entire designated possibly infinite set. Identity is retained in the generating set. Compare two proper-parabolic representatives; ambient equalities give exactly the required intersection. The elementary rank-two case is handled separately.

clauses.claim: All admissible kernels together generate K.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: For every interval relation choose two consecutive sufficiently large exponents. Both normal closures are admissible and contained in K; their join contains the relation. Normal generation yields the equality.

clauses.claim: Unique minimal regular cover is equivalent to C-group monodromy, for every finite rank.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Unique maximal admissible subgroup contains every admissible subgroup and hence equals K. Conversely admissible K is the greatest subgroup. Ranks0,1 are trivial; rank2 flags give a cycle or double line. Infinite flag sets do not change the argument.

clauses.claim: The machine-checked scope is five elementary new theorems and six retained theorems.
clauses.reviewed_supplied_argument: Read the actual statements and proofs. Normal generation and consecutive-power supply are explicit hypotheses; geometry and the polytope correspondence are not formalized. Three rejected altered proofs and four independent countermodels test meaningful hypotheses.

not_claimed: Finiteness of the newly supplied covers or minimal descendants.
Infinitely many minimal covers for every non-C monodromy.
Formal verification of the full geometric proof.
